title: API Gateway
description: Build an API gateway with route matching, service aggregation, response composition, caching, and rate limiting.

steps.title: Create route registry
steps.description: Define a `Route` data structure with: `method` (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE), `path` (string like '/users/:id'), `target` (object with service and endpoint), and `middleware` (array of function names). Create a `RouteRegistry` class that stores routes and provides `register(route)`. Register 5 routes for users, products, orders, payments, and health. Print the complete route table.
hints: Store routes in an array for ordered matching or a Map keyed by method+path
Route targets describe backend services, e.g. { service: 'user-service', endpoint: '/users/:id' }
Print the route table as a formatted list: 'GET /users/:id -> user-service/users/:id'

verification.successMessage: Route registry correctly stores and displays all registered routes with their targets!
verification.failureMessage: Print the route table showing method, path, and target service for each registered route.

steps.title: Implement route matching
steps.description: Build a `matchRoute(method, path)` method that finds the matching route for an incoming request. Support path parameters with `:param` syntax (e.g. '/users/:id' matches '/users/42' with params { id: '42' }). Convert route patterns to regex for matching. Print the matched route template and extracted path parameters for several test requests.
hints: Convert '/users/:id' to regex: replace ':param' with '([^/]+)' named capture groups
Iterate registered routes and return the first match with extracted params
Print 'Matched: GET /users/42 -> /users/:id, params: { id: "42" }'

verification.successMessage: Route matching correctly resolves paths with parameters and extracts values!
verification.failureMessage: Print the matched route and extracted parameters for each test request.

steps.title: Add request transformation
steps.description: Implement a request transformation pipeline. Create middleware functions that modify the request before forwarding: `addHeaders(req)` adds API key and timestamp, `transformBody(req)` converts field names to camelCase, `validateParams(req)` checks required params exist. Chain these in a `TransformMiddleware` class. Print the transformed request object at each stage.
hints: Each middleware is a function: (request) => modifiedRequest or throws on validation error
Chain them sequentially: request -> addHeaders -> transformBody -> validateParams -> final
Print 'After <middleware>: <transformed request fields>' at each stage

verification.successMessage: Request transformation pipeline correctly modifies requests through each middleware stage!
verification.failureMessage: Print the request state after each middleware transformation showing what was added or modified.

steps.title: Implement service aggregation
steps.description: Create an `Aggregator` that calls multiple backend services (simulated with async functions) and combines their responses. For an order detail endpoint, aggregate data from user-service (user info), product-service (product details), and payment-service (payment status). Simulate each service call with a delay and return mock data. Print the aggregated response combining all three service results.
hints: Simulate services as async functions: getUser(userId) returns { id, name, email } after N ms
Use Promise.all() to call independent services in parallel for faster aggregation
Print 'Aggregated response: { user: {...}, products: [...], payment: {...} }'

verification.successMessage: Service aggregation correctly calls multiple services and combines their responses!
verification.failureMessage: Print the full aggregated response showing user, products, and payment data combined.

steps.title: Add response caching
steps.description: Implement a response cache that stores responses by request URL (method + path + query). Support configurable `ttlMs` per route. Add `getCachedResponse(key)` and `setCachedResponse(key, response, ttlMs)` methods. On an incoming request, check cache first before forwarding to the backend. Print cache hit/miss status for repeated requests to the same endpoint.
hints: Use a Map with key = 'GET:/users/42' and value = { data, expiry, cachedAt }
Check if cached response exists and is not expired before returning it
Print 'Cache HIT: GET /users/42 (served from cache)' or 'Cache MISS: GET /users/42 (forwarding)'

verification.test: output.includes('CACHE HIT') && output.includes('CACHE MISS') && output.includes('served from cache')
verification.successMessage: Response caching correctly serves cached responses on hit and forwards on miss!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'CACHE HIT' or 'CACHE MISS' for each request showing whether it was served from cache or forwarded.

steps.title: Implement rate limiting per route
steps.description: Add configurable rate limiting per route. Each route can have a rate limit config: `{ maxRequests: number, windowMs: number }`. Use a sliding window log per route. Create a `RateLimiter` class integrated with the gateway that checks limits before processing. Print 'ALLOWED' or 'BLOCKED (429)' for each request along with remaining quota for the route.
hints: Store rate limit state per route: rateLimits[routeKey] = { timestamps: [], maxRequests, windowMs }
Filter out expired timestamps on each check and compare count to maxRequests
Print 'GET /users/:id -> ALLOWED (24/30 remaining)' or 'BLOCKED (0/30 remaining, 429)'

verification.successMessage: Per-route rate limiting correctly allows requests under the limit and blocks with 429!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'ALLOWED (N remaining)' or 'BLOCKED (429)' for each request showing remaining quota.

steps.title: Build response composition
steps.description: Create a response composer that merges multiple service responses into a single API response with proper error handling. Each service response includes: `{ status, data, error }`. The composer should merge successful responses, collect errors, and return `{ statusCode, body: { data, errors }, headers }`. Test with a mix of successful and failing services and print the composed response.
hints: Aggregate successful responses into response.data grouped by source: data: { user: {...}, products: [...] }
Collect errors with source info: errors: [{ service: 'payment-service', error: 'timeout', status: 502 }]
Set statusCode to 200 if all succeeded, or highest error status if any failed

verification.successMessage: Response composer correctly merges multiple service results with error handling!
verification.failureMessage: Print the full composed response showing statusCode, data from each service, and any errors collected.
